Definition: from G2205; to have warmth of feeling for or against:--affect, covet (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be) zealous(-ly affect).
BiblicalUsage: Zeloo is to burn with desire for something, to covet it earnestly, whether for good or for evil. Paul tells the Corinthians to covet earnestly the best gifts and to follow after love and desire spiritual gifts, and he tells them his own jealousy over them is the jealousy of God, guarding a bride for her husband. Paul tells the Galatians it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, so the fire itself is not the enemy; the question is what it is aimed at.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe zeal is a fire that must be aimed, because the same heat that purifies can also burn the house down. Paul's godly jealousy protects the church, and the envy of his opponents tries to steal it, and the difference is not the heat but the heart behind it. My position is that we should covet the best gifts and desire what God desires, and let that fire keep us faithful instead of making us bitter.
